newsitem.title: USA: Providers see problems in Boston Edison/EUA deal.
newsitem.headline: Providers see problems in Boston Edison/EUA deal.

text.p: A group of independent power providers, generators and marketers objected on Tuesday to the pending agreement between Boston Edison and Eastern Utilities Associates which does not deal with nuclear power generation.

The deal, approved by Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harbarger, must still be approved by the state's Department of Public Utilities and does not address the nuclear generation capacity of Boston Edison, which operates the 670-megawatt Pilgrim nuclear power plant.

"If Boston Edison does not divest itself of nuclear power-generation plants, we wonder if ratepayer dollars would then be used to subsidize these operations at the expense of a true competitive market," said Alyse Gray, co-chair of the Competitive Power Coalition, a Massachusetts-based organization of competitive power providers.

Dan Alligretti, who is on the CPC board and works for Enron Corp, the largest wholesale trader of electricity in the United States, said he had not seen the agreement, which he termed "a letter of intent, a set of principles."
"We're concerned that if Boston Edison keeps Pilgrim than it will not a totally neutral situation," Alligretti said in a telephone interview.
Alligretti, whose company is in talks to acquire Portland General Electric Co, said he could not say if Enron was uninterested in acquiring Pilgrim. "It would depend on the price," he said.

A deregulation deal announced in September between Massachusetts Electric and other power companies to divest their generation assets will come up for formal review before the public utilities department Jan 10.
